text: Last time we finished Level Five.
You learned six spelling rules, and you learned them all.
Today we are starting Level Six, and this one is different.
Today you are not learning a rule.
Today you are learning a trick — a trick that lets you read a whole pile of words at once.
Let me show you what I mean.
Now watch what happens when I change just ONE letter.
Only the front changed, and it made a brand new word.
And once you know it, you can read hundreds of words.
Look at the end of the word.
The last two letters are a and t.
Now here is the important part.
Every word that ends in those two letters says At.
So all I have to do is put a different letter in front, and I get another word I can read.
I will keep At and change only the front.
And you only had to learn one ending.
That is called a word family.
All those words are in the At family, because they all end the same way.
Let's keep the same vowel and change the ending.
It is still a short a, just like At.
The a stays put every single time.
It is only the letters around it that move.
This time it is a short e.
Five words, and the same trick worked again.
We have three families here, so listen carefully to the ending each time.
All three of those families have the same vowel.
Only the letter at the end did.
Listen to the middle of every one of those words.
It is the same o sound every time.
Our last short vowel is u.
That is twelve more words from two endings.
Now I want to show you one more family, but I have to be honest with you about it, because it does not work quite the same way.
Change the front letter, get a new word.
That is not a short a.
It does not say the short a sound like Cat.
It has changed into something else.
So we do not sound this family out letter by letter.
We learn the whole ending in one piece.
When you see those three letters together, a, l, l, you say All.
That is the Floss rule from Level Five — one clap, short vowel, ends in l, so we double it.
Now it is your turn, and this is exactly what the app will ask you.
I am going to show you a word, and you tell me which letter goes at the front.
And the picture is a bug.
Find the ending you know, then work out the front.
Let's say what we learned today.
A word family is a group of words that all end the same way.
If you can read the ending, you can read every word in the family.
You only have to change the letter at the front.
Today you met thirteen families, and you read eighty-one words.
That is what makes this trick so useful.
I am really proud of you.
This is the skill that turns sounding out into reading.
Next time we will keep going with Level Six and practise these families until they are easy.
